title: Offside
subtitle: Interactive simulator · Drag all five players to see the line change.
direction: The blue team attacks to the right →
involved: The receiver plays the ball or interferes with play
footnote: The ball moves with the blue passer. Player markers simplify the law: actual judgments use all body parts that can legally play the ball (not hands or arms). Simply being in an offside position is not an offence unless the player becomes involved as specified in Law 11.
offline: Works offline without AI services. Official law:
offenseDetail: At the moment of the pass, the receiver is in the opponents’ half and nearer the goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent. Playing the pass results in an indirect free kick.
positionOnlyDetail: The receiver is in an offside position when the pass is played, but does not become involved or interfere with an opponent in this example.
ownDetail: The receiver is in their own half or on the halfway line, where they cannot be in an offside position.
ballDetail: The receiver is level with or behind the ball, even if there are no opponents ahead.
defDetail: The receiver is level with or behind the second-last opponent, including the goalkeeper.
otherDetail: The position relative to the ball allows the pass to be received.
loadError: The application could not start. Reload the page to retry.
